transcript.content:
hey, i'm Berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey Berry! ok so the bit that really stuck with me was my old teacher Mr Hale turning into a huge orange octopus while he was writing on the board 😅 he still had the chalk in one arm. the whole school was underwater, it was my primary school

ha, still holding the chalk though. he wasn't letting that go

what did he do once he'd turned?

haha no, he wasn't letting go of it 😂 honestly i don't remember him doing anything after, the school bell rang pretty much straight away. but it came out as a big stream of bubbles going up to the surface, and all the other pupils swam out the window at once. they were all fish btw, little silver fish at the desks

the bell coming out as bubbles is so good. and a whole class of little silver fish just going out the window at once

were you one of the fish too?
i don't remember being a fish tbh. i could breathe fine underwater and i swam down the corridor instead of walking. when they all went out the window i tried to follow them but then i woke up

ah, right as you went to follow them. and swimming down the corridor instead of walking

how did it feel being back there underwater, did it stay the same the whole way through?

honestly i don't really remember how i felt about it. but it looked the same the whole time, all murky blue and green, like looking through a fish tank that needs cleaning. and the light came down in wobbly beams from above. the desks in the classroom were covered in seaweed too

a fish tank that needs cleaning, i can see that. and seaweed all over the desks

was there anything in there that felt like it mattered? like the chalk, or something else, or nothing really
not really, nothing felt like it meant anything that i remember. the chalk just stuck with me cause it was funny. oh and before he turned he was just normal Mr Hale in his brown jacket

normal Mr Hale in his brown jacket, then suddenly octopus

do you remember how it started? like was the school already underwater when you got there
yeah i think it was just already underwater, i don't remember getting there or it starting. i was just back at the school and it was like that

that's fine, you were just there and it was already like that

so here's what i've got. you were back at your old primary school and the whole place was underwater. it was murky blue and green, like looking through a fish tank that needs cleaning, with wobbly beams of light coming down from above and seaweed all over the desks. you could breathe fine and you swam down the corridor instead of walking. the other pupils were little silver fish sitting at the desks. Mr Hale was just normal Mr Hale in his brown jacket, writing on the board, and then he turned into a huge orange octopus, still holding the chalk in one arm. then the bell rang, but it came out as a big stream of bubbles going up to the surface, and all the fish swam out the window at once. you tried to follow them, and then you woke up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it exactly, you got all of it 😊 nothing missing that i can think of

ah good, i'm glad

would you like to see it drawn?
oh yeah i'd love that!! especially mr hale as the octopus with the chalk 😂

ha yes, the chalk has to be in there

here are a few ways it could look. soft watercolour, loose and gentle like a picture book left out in the rain. a hand-cut paper collage, playful and flat like a class art project come to life. an old children's book print, warm and nostalgic like a book you'd remember from primary school. or a photograph, real and a bit cloudy, like peering through a fish tank that needs cleaning

which feels closest? or you can tell me your own way
the photograph one i think, the cloudy fish tank look is how it actually looked

yeah, the photograph feels right for it

i'll start with mr hale. i'm picturing him as he was before he turned, just an ordinary middle-aged man in his brown jacket. the ordinary middle-aged bit is my guess, since you didn't say

is anything about him different from that, or would you leave it to me?
yeah the brown jacket's right. i don't really remember what he looked like apart from that, so go with your guess, that sounds fine

ok, i'm sketching mr hale and the school corridor and the chalk now, they'll show up on the right

for the classroom on its own, i'm picturing wobbly beams of light coming down from above through murky blue-green water. the rest is my guess: a primary school classroom, completely underwater, with the board at the front, desks facing it covered in seaweed, and the window

is anything different from that, or would you leave it to me?
yeah that sounds right. the seaweed on the desks and the light beams are how i remember it. i don't really remember the rest of the room so go with your guess

ok, sketching the classroom now

everything's being sketched and it'll show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
ooh they're all up! yeah they look right to me, that's pretty much how it was 😊

ah good, i'm really glad

mr hale in his brown jacket, the seaweed desks, the chalk. if anything starts looking off to you later, just say
will do, thanks Berry! it's kinda funny seeing mr hale like that 😂

ha, he'd probably have something to say about it

everything's sketched now, so i'll start drawing the dream itself, moment by moment in order, each one carrying on from the last. they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ooh exciting! i can see the first couple, they look right so far 😊 can't wait to see the octopus one

ah good. swimming down the corridor, then mr hale in his brown jacket at the board

the next four carry on from there, so the octopus is coming. they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i'll keep an eye out for them! those first two look right, the corridor especially 😊

ah good, glad the corridor feels right

the other four are still on their way, they'll pop up on the right soon
oh there's a third one now! looks right to me 😊 waiting on the octopus haha

that third one is the octopus actually, mr hale at the board with the chalk still in one arm

the last three carry on from him, so i'll draw those once you're happy with this one. is that how you saw him?
oh haha yeah that's him! huge orange octopus with the chalk, that's exactly how i saw him 😂 go ahead with the rest

ha, good, that's him

i'm really sorry, though. two of the moments couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side: the bell coming out as bubbles, and all the little fish swimming out the window. that's on us, not anything you did

there's one more still on its way, and it'll show up on the right soon
aw that's a shame, the bubbles bell was one of my favourite bits 😅 but no worries, not your fault. the new one looks right to me, i'll wait for the last one

yeah, i'm sorry about the bubbles bell, that was one of my favourites too

that new one is actually the last one: you swimming toward the window to follow the fish, right before you woke up

does it look the way you remember that last moment?
yeah that's pretty much it, me going for the window after them. looks right 😊 bit weird without the fish going out first but i get it

yeah, it does feel a bit odd with the fish missing just before it. i'm sorry about that, and about the bubbles bell, those two not being drawn was a problem on our side

four of the six moments are there on the right, from the corridor through to you heading for the window. thanks for sharing this one with me, mr hale and his chalk especially. you can look through it all there whenever you like

turns.rule: 2: story understood and told to the end
turns.brief:
Move: retell. You have their dream. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right or missed anything.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: R1: retelling confirmed
turns.brief:
Move: offer_visualize. They've confirmed you have their dream. Ask them, simply and warmly, whether they'd like to see it drawn. One question. Don't explain how it works.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: O1: they want to see it
turns.brief:
Move: choose_style. They want to see it. Offer these ways it could be drawn, each in a few plain words, and ask which feels closest, or whether they'd describe their own: a) soft watercolour: Loose and gentle, like a picture book left out in the rain.; b) a hand-cut paper collage: Playful and flat, like a class art project come to life.; c) an old children's book print: Nostalgic and warm, like a book you remember from primary school.; d) a photograph: Real and a bit cloudy, like peering through a fish tank that needs cleaning..
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: S1: they chose how it looks
turns.brief:
Move: start. They chose a photograph. Say you'll start with mr hale, then describe how you picture mr hale on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: who they are: the dreamer's old primary school teacher; wears: brown jacket. You filled in (say plainly that these are your guesses): looks: an ordinary middle-aged man. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: B1: profile you_choose — next one
turns.brief:
Move: confirm_profile. First say, in a few words, that you're sketching mr hale and the school corridor and the chalk now and it'll appear on the right: only that, nothing else is being drawn yet. Then describe how you picture the classroom on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: light: wobbly beams from above through murky blue-green water. You filled in (say plainly that these are your guesses): what kind of place: a primary school classroom, inside, completely underwater, with the board at the front and desks facing it; what's in it: the board, desks covered in seaweed, the window. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: B1: profile you_choose — all profiles settled
turns.brief:
Move: build_done. Say you're sketching the classroom now. Tell them everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. They can say if anything looks wrong once it's there. Keep it short; no question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. mr hale and the other pupils and the school corridor and the classroom and the chalk are up on the right now: ask if it looks the way they remember.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V3: every sketch settled — on to the moments
turns.brief:
Move: sheets_done. Take in that they're happy with mr hale and the school corridor and the classroom and the chalk. Everyone and everything is sketched now. Tell them you'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready. No question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>
